Priya Patel: Hey team — quick handoff. We had a multi-regional failover triggered to us-east due to GCP egress flap. Customer-facing latency spiked ~10x for ~12m. I paged primary. ops-bot: INCIDENT AUTO-PAGER: P50/P95 latency breach on /v1/generate (region: eu-west1 -> failover to us-east). PagerID: #P-8792 :rotating_light:
Marco Diaz: I'm primary on this shift, taking lead. Currently confirming if failover was automatic or manual. Starting investigation. @Dana can you check routing table push? :eyes:
Dana Chen: on it — checking rollout history... looks like k8s egress policy updated 23:44 UTC, rollback in progress now. Logs show 502s from network-proxy.
Marco Diaz: Thanks. @Liu can you check KV cache pressure and batcher queues? We saw token generation slowdowns earlier.
Liu Wang: KV cache read latency increased from 2ms -> 120ms around 23:46. Cache hit rate dropped ~27%. Possibly cross-region memcache eviction due to node restart.
Marco Diaz: Ok—probable cascade: network egress issue triggered node restarts -> cache pressure -> higher latency -> automatic failover to us-east. Customer impact: short-lived 5-15m increased latencies and some 502s for eu-west customers. No data loss.
Priya Patel: Noted. Reproduction: hit /v1/generate with streaming enabled during the window and saw stalls followed by reconnects. We applied canary rollback in eu-west at 23:50 which reduced errors.
Dana Chen: Rollback completed 23:52. k8s events: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/network-proxy -n prod --to-revision=42` worked. Command output snip:
```
deployment "network-proxy" rolled back to revision 42
```
Marco Diaz: Actions taken: rolled back proxy, scaled up memcache replicas +2 (temporarily), and disabled aggressive autoscaler policy for memcache. All changes tracked in incident doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-8792 (internal link)
ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity downgraded to P2 at 23:54 UTC — failover heal observed. Metrics: p95 latency returned to baseline by 23:58.
Priya Patel: Current status: eu-west stable, us-east still serving some fallback traffic but routing normalized. No open customer tickets yet, but support flagged two customers in eu-west reporting errors (cust-247, cust-601).
Jordan Blake: I'll take follow-up with Support for cust-247 and cust-601, confirm whether they saw data issues or just transient errors. Planning to send proactive note if needed.
Marco Diaz: Next steps for the night shift: 1) Monitor KV hit rate and memcache eviction logs for 3 hours 2) Revert temporary memcache scaling once stable 3) Add circuit-breaker in routing to prevent automatic regional failover on single-proxy errors (tracking RFC in eng-runtime backlog)
Priya Patel: Handoff: I'm handing primary to Jordan at 00:05 UTC. Jordan will be primary, Marco remains secondary for 2h. Dana please be on-call for quick rollback assistance. Ops runbook refs: https://docs.redwood.com/runbooks/network-egress-failover.md and `runbook:memcache-eviction` (internal)
Jordan Blake: Acknowledged — taking primary at 00:05 UTC. I'll watch p95, KV hit rate, and error budget dashboard. If anything flares, page Marco and Priya. :thumbsup:
Marco Diaz: Quick note for morning crew: add postmortem template entries for "egress policy rollout checks" and "memcache scale sensitivity". I'll start the postmortem draft; tag SRE and eng-runtime.
Priya Patel: Closing notes: No SLA breaches expected for this event but still documenting. If anyone spots related anomalies in other regions, alert in this thread. Signing off for a few mins while I handoff. :wave:
